A series from The One Percent

The Focus Tax

Deep reads on what an unstructured day really costs.

Every open loop, every decision you make twice, every meeting you try to hold in your head charges you a little. These essays are about that tax: what it costs, why trying harder never pays it, and the structure that does.

Anthony Brown Sr.
4 essays · about 37 minutes in all · free for members
  1. 001 The Tab You Never Closed You did not avoid the hard thing by doing nothing. You avoided it with real work, and that is exactly why the escape worked. 9 min read

  3. 003 How to Run a Meeting When Your Brain Won’t Stay in the Room You are not bad at meetings. You are trying to hold a whole hour in a space that was built to hold about four things at once. 9 min read
  4. 004 You Do Not Need More Focus, You Need Fewer Decisions The work is not what wore you down. Deciding what to work on, forty times before lunch, is what wore you down. 10 min read
